query: Why do some incidents take longer to resolve?

per_column.name: resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: This is the magnitude of the delay outcome itself (how long resolution took), not a constitutive aspect/reason of the delay. It restates the whole 'delay' rather than decomposing its reasons.

per_column.name: priority_numeric
per_column.rationale: Priority is an attribute of the incident that may correlate with or predict delay, but it is not a part-of the concept 'delay reasons'; it is an external driver.

per_column.name: category_mismatch
per_column.rationale: A misclassified category could be a potential cause of delay, but a cause is not a constitutive facet (an aspect OF) of the delay-reasons concept.

per_column.name: opened_hour
per_column.rationale: Time of day the incident opened is a contextual predictor, not an aspect that constitutes the reasons for delay.

per_column.name: opened_day_of_week
per_column.rationale: Day of week is a temporal covariate/predictor of delay, not a constitutive part of the delay-reasons concept.

per_column.name: is_weekend
per_column.rationale: Weekend flag is a derived temporal predictor of delay, overlapping with opened_day_of_week, and not a facet of the concept itself.

judge.rationale: None of the added columns are constitutive facets (parts-of) the concept 'incident_delay_reasons'. A proper faceted decomposition would carve delay reasons into non-overlapping aspects such as triage/assignment delay, waiting-on-requester delay, vendor/third-party delay, technical diagnosis/effort, approval/change-control delay, and resource/queue contention. Instead the columns are the delay outcome itself (resolution_hours = restatement), external predictors (priority, opened_hour, opened_day_of_week, is_weekend), and a potential cause (category_mismatch). The temporal columns also overlap (is_weekend is derived from opened_day_of_week). Since there are zero true facets, both mutual exclusivity and exhaustiveness with respect to the concept score 0.
